A1.justification: Both PDFs describe One-to-All Animation and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A-E. Additions, reformatting, and renumbering can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original TikTok, Cartoon, and DeepFashion evaluations, component ablations, a user study, and supplementary experimental results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and reports an expanded user study, quantitative misalignment ablations, and additional visual comparisons.

M1.justification: The outpainting procedure, Reference Extractor, hybrid attention, pose control, token replacement, losses, and training stages remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies facial-only augmentation, which v1 already specified in Section 4.3; this does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Training sources and TikTok, Cartoon, and DeepFashion coverage are retained. The expanded study and additional illustrations concern existing misaligned animation scenarios and human/cartoon/anime domains; additional samples do not introduce a distinct task or population.

E2.justification: The new quantitative misalignment ablation includes UniAnimate-DiT as an AED comparator in v3 Table 4. It already appeared in v1's benchmark and qualitative comparisons, but the earlier quantitative component ablation contained only internal variants. Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported user study from 5 characters, 6 driving videos, 30 cases, and 4 participants to 10 characters, 10 videos, 100 cases, and 30 participants. Section 4.3 additionally evaluates 100 misaligned pairs using CSIM, AED, and APD-body, substantially expanding the protocol for assessing misalignment.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends the existing identity-control ablation by quantifying identity, body-pose, and expression effects of facial augmentation and reference-guided control. Figures 17-18 add misaligned-input comparisons with Wan-Animate. Existing extractor, token-replacement, RoPE, training-stage, outpainting, and guidance analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The increased participant and case counts change sample sizes, not uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: For the expanded user study, unseen-region win/loss percentages change from 50.8/25.8 to 47.6/28.1, and seen-region percentages from 69.2/19.2 to 72.4/16.1; these are different-setting results. New Table 4 reports full-control CSIM 0.8172 and AED 0.7457, versus 0.6761 and 0.6898 without identity-robust control. Additional visual results appear in Figures 17-18. Tables 1-3 and retained appendix table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The attention, rectified-flow, guidance, token-replacement, and weighted-loss mathematics remain equivalent. Equations are compacted and renumbered, including equivalent notation for temporal RoPE set to zero. The added conventional metric descriptions do not introduce a new theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: unified image/video generation under misalignment, identity-preserving reference extraction, identity-robust pose control, and coherent long-video generation. Added evaluations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly acknowledges an expression-accuracy tradeoff from facial augmentation and argues that retaining facial signals preserves expressions better than discarding them. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning separate image/video checkpoints, computational cost, and camera control.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds ArcFace, SMIRK, and head-excluded DWPose measurement details. The abstract changes code/model access from a future promise to reported availability, although the appendix still promises evaluation-code release. Section 3.3 removes explicit relative-position and bone-length-ratio details from the augmentation description. Architecture, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to ArcFace, LivePortrait, SMIRK, and First Order Motion Model to support the new evaluation metrics. The positioning against spatially aligned and task-specific generation methods remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 2.2 and 3.3 receive localized condensation and rewriting, alongside grammatical and terminology corrections. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact; the limitations section is retained rather than newly introduced.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 4 and two comparison plates, Figures 17-18, and redraws Figure 7's preference charts. The previous Cartoon Figure 17 becomes Figure 19. Equation compaction and text reflow alter placement, while the existing visual organization is largely retained.

improvement.justification: The larger user study and new quantitative misalignment ablation strengthen evidence for the central identity-control claim and expose its expression-accuracy tradeoff. Metric implementation details and additional visual comparisons improve assessability. These focused gains outweigh the modest loss of augmentation detail, while the main method and established benchmark results remain unchanged.
